# RestPilot iPhone app: White Glove readiness

**Dated 15 Nov 2026.** Snapshot, not live status. Built with Amber's White Glove Treatment project (`ios-app/`, generated by `amberai src/lib/api-v1/ios-build`) and tested only in the free iOS **simulator** on GitHub's macOS runners. **Nothing was signed, uploaded, submitted or paid for. Nothing was tested on a physical iPhone.**

Companion documents: `NATIVE-APP.md` (architecture and native features), `WEARABLES.md` (Apple Health and other providers). Amber's own notes: amberai `docs/white-glove-treatment/RESTPILOT-APP.md` and `OWNER-SETUP.md` (read 14 Nov 2026).

## 2. App Review Guidelines (quoted from developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines, read 14 Nov 2026; the page shows no date)

- **4.2 Minimum Functionality:** "Your app should include features, content, and UI that elevate it beyond a repackaged website. If your app is not particularly useful, unique, or "app-like," it doesn't belong on the App Store." 4.2.2: apps "shouldn't primarily be marketing materials, advertisements, web clippings, content aggregators, or a collection of links."
  *Assessment:* much better than a wrapper now, still a risk. The app adds things the website cannot do: reminders scheduled on the phone that fire offline and with the app closed, read-only Apple Health sleep and HRV that change the on-phone plan, an offline screen with the person's next shifts, and notification deep links. Most screens are still web content. Strongest next steps (`NATIVE-APP.md` §7): photograph-a-roster import, then a Lock Screen widget.
- **3.1.1 In-App Purchase:** "If you want to unlock features or functionality within your app, (by way of example: subscriptions, …), you must use in-app purchase." *Assessment:* blocked while restpilotai.com serves the Lovable Stripe paywall (item 13).
- **5.1.1(v) Account Sign-In:** "If your app supports account creation, you must also offer account deletion within the app." *Assessment:* met (item 12).
- **5.1.2(i) Data Use and Sharing:** "You must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, including with third-party AI, and obtain explicit permission before doing so." *Assessment:* disclosure exists; explicit in-app permission does not (item 14).
- **5.1.3 Health and Health Research:** (i) health data, "including from … HealthKit API", may not be used or disclosed "for advertising, marketing, or other use-based data mining purposes other than improving health management, or for the purpose of health research, and then only with permission", and "You must disclose the specific health data that you are collecting from the device." (ii) apps "may not store personal health information in iCloud." *Assessment:* Apple Health data is read only after Connect, stays in the app's own storage on the phone (no iCloud, no server, no AI, no ads), and the Connect card names the three data types. The privacy policy still needs the paragraph in §3.

## 3. Owner approvals

**Purpose strings (Info.plist), all drafts:**

| Key | Draft wording | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` | "RestPilot uses the microphone only while you talk to your AI sleep coach." | Voice coach. Without it iOS closes the app. |
| `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` | "RestPilot uses your location to show local weather and commute times for your shift plan." | Weather and commute. |
| `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` | "RestPilot reads your sleep, heart rate variability and resting heart rate from Apple Health to tailor your sleep plan around your shifts. It never writes to Apple Health, and this data stays on your iPhone." | Apple Health (PR #17). |

Not needed: notifications (local notifications have no purpose string), `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription` (the app never writes), camera and photos (not used yet).

**Privacy policy paragraph (draft, for `/legal/privacy`):** "Apple Health. In the RestPilot iPhone app you can choose to connect Apple Health. If you do, RestPilot reads your sleep analysis, heart rate variability and resting heart rate, only to tailor your sleep plan and recommendations. This data stays on your iPhone, in the RestPilot app's own storage (included in your iPhone's device backup like other app data): it is not sent to RestPilot's servers or to the AI coach, it is not used for advertising or marketing, RestPilot does not store it in iCloud, and it is not sold or shared. RestPilot never writes to Apple Health. Disconnect in Profile deletes RestPilot's copy; you can also remove access in the Settings app under Health → Data Access & Devices → RestPilot."

## 4. Amber's pipeline: what runs, what does not

- **Simulator lane: runs.** `.github/workflows/ios-simulator.yml` is the pipeline's own GitHub simulator lane pointed at `ios-app/`; it passed on PR #7 and PR #13 with the plugins. `ios-native-e2e.yml` adds the end-to-end checks on top (CI only).
- **TestFlight lane: gap.** The handoff (`handoff.ts`, `prepareIosProjectTree`) does not build the committed `ios-app/` tree. It regenerates a project from a wrap package: `npm install`, `cap add ios`, `cap sync ios`, Info.plist additions, bundle id, the package icon. From this repo's work, that path:
  - **keeps** the npm plugins, `capacitor.config.json` (errorPath, splash settings), `www/` (offline screen) and the icon (`ios/AppIcon-1024.png`, format accepted);
  - **drops** the launch images, `App.entitlements` and `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS` (HealthKit), and the local `plugins/restpilot-health` folder;
  - **refuses** `NSHealthShareUsageDescription`: `controls.ts` accepts only microphone, camera, location, speech recognition and photo library keys (`usageDescriptions.NSHealthShareUsageDescription is not a supported purpose-string key`).
- **Smallest Amber change that closes it (for the owner to approve in amberai; not done here):** a "prebuilt project" input for the handoff that pushes a committed Capacitor tree (this `ios-app/`) to `wrap/<jobId>` unchanged, keeping every existing control (private build repo, authorized team check, declarations, draft-string refusal, no submission). Alternative: extend the package format with `ios/overlay/**` (entitlements, assets, local plugins) and add `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` to `USAGE_DESCRIPTION_KEYS`.
- Until then, the existing GitHub fallback's signed workflow would need the owner's App Store Connect key and team (`OWNER-SETUP.md` §1–5, §9).

## 5. App Store Connect, In-App Purchase and RevenueCat (owner-only, no Apple calls made here)

Owner decision (15 Nov): Apple purchasing stays **disabled** until sandbox verification is complete. The app already carries the RevenueCat plugin (`@revenuecat/purchases-capacitor` 9.2.2, the Capacitor 6 line) and the In-App Purchase capability, inert without keys (PR #28); every IAP flag from #16 (`IAP_ENABLED`, `IAP_HONOR_SANDBOX`, `VITE_IAP_ENABLED`) stays unset/false. The products below match `ios-app/ios/App/RestPilot.storekit` (PR #27), which the simulator uses for local StoreKit testing. Steps, from Apple's help pages (read 15 Nov 2026); `SUBSCRIPTIONS.md` §7 has the RevenueCat, webhook and secrets detail.

**A. Agreements (Account Holder; once)**

1. App Store Connect → Business: accept the latest **Apple Developer Program License Agreement** (needed before any app record).
2. Same page → Agreements: accept the **Paid Applications** agreement, then add **banking** and complete **tax** forms. Subscriptions cannot be sold, or even tested in sandbox reliably, until all three show "Active".
3. Optional: apply to the App Store Small Business Program (15% instead of 30%).

**B. Register the bundle ID** ([Register an App ID](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/identifiers/register-an-app-id/); Account Holder or Admin)

1. developer.apple.com → Account → Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles → Identifiers → **+**.
2. Select **App IDs** → Continue → type **App** → Continue.
3. Description `RestPilot`; Bundle ID **Explicit** `com.restpilotai.app` (must match `ios-app/capacitor.config.json` and the Xcode project exactly).
4. Capabilities: tick **HealthKit** (leave Clinical Health Records and Background Delivery off; the app only reads, in the foreground). In-App Purchase "is enabled by default for an explicit App ID" and cannot be unticked. Leave Associated Domains for later (universal links, `NATIVE-APP.md` §4).
5. Continue → Register.

**C. Create the app record** ([Add a new app](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/create-an-app-record/add-a-new-app))

1. App Store Connect → Apps → **+** → **New App**.
2. Platforms **iOS**; Name `RestPilot` (if taken, e.g. `RestPilot AI`; 30 characters max, shown on the App Store); Primary Language English (U.S.); Bundle ID choose `com.restpilotai.app` from the menu (it appears only after step B); SKU `restpilot-ios-1` (internal, permanent); User Access **Full Access** → **Create**.
3. App Information: category Health & Fitness; Privacy Policy URL `https://restpilotai.com/legal/privacy`.

**D. Subscriptions** ([Offer auto-renewable subscriptions](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/offer-auto-renewable-subscriptions))

1. The RestPilot app → Monetization → **Subscriptions** → Subscription Groups **+**: reference name `RestPilot Premium` → Create.
2. In the group, **Create** a subscription: reference name `Annual`, Product ID **`restpilot_annual`** → Create. Set Subscription Duration **1 Year**; Availability: all countries/regions (or the owner's list); Subscription Prices **+** → United States **USD 49.99** → let Apple calculate the other storefronts (review them) → Confirm.
3. **Create** a second subscription: reference name `Monthly`, Product ID **`restpilot_monthly`** → Duration **1 Month** → price **USD 7.99**, same availability.
4. **Intro offer, on each of the two** ([Set up introductory offers](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/set-up-introductory-offers-for-auto-renewable-subscriptions)): Subscription Prices → **+** → **Create Introductory Offer** → countries: all → start date today, **no end date** → type **Free** → duration **2 Weeks** → Confirm. Offers cannot be edited, only ended and recreated. Each Apple Account gets one introductory offer per subscription group.
5. Group order: drag **Annual above Monthly** (level 1), so a switch between them is an upgrade/downgrade, not a second subscription.
6. Localizations: the group (display name `RestPilot Premium`) and each product (display name `Annual` / `Monthly`, a one-line description), English (U.S.).
7. Review Information on each product: a screenshot of the in-app paywall (take it from a TestFlight build with IAP on in staging, step F) and review notes.
8. Product IDs are permanent and can never be reused. Use exactly these two: the code and the `.storekit` file match them. The products stay "Missing Metadata" / "Ready to Submit" until they are attached to an app version; Apple: "Your first auto-renewable subscription must be submitted with a new app version."

**E. Sandbox testers and keys**

1. Users and Access → **Sandbox** → Test Accounts **+**: two sandbox Apple Accounts (new e-mail addresses never used for an Apple Account).
2. Users and Access → Integrations → **In-App Purchase** → generate a key; download the `.p8` once and give it, with its Key ID and Issuer ID, to RevenueCat only.
3. RevenueCat (owner's account): project, App Store app `com.restpilotai.app`, import both products, entitlement `premium` with both attached, offering marked Current, webhook to `https://<railway host>/api/public/iap/revenuecat` with HMAC signing (`SUBSCRIPTIONS.md` §7 steps 7–9). Secrets go only into Railway's variable editor. The public `appl_…` SDK key goes into the site's build environment, never into `ios-app/`.

**F. Sandbox verification (before any flag is turned on in production)**

On a signed TestFlight build on a **physical iPhone** (none was done in this work), signed in to a sandbox account, with the flags on in **staging only**: buy Monthly and Annual, the 2-week trial (accelerated in sandbox), cancel in Settings, Restore on a second account, and RevenueCat "Send test event" returning 200 with `store_entitlements` updated. Only then repeat for production (`SUBSCRIPTIONS.md` §7 steps 13–14).

**User-agent token.** The app identifies itself to the server and site with `RestPilotApp/<version>` at the end of the WebView user agent (`appendUserAgent` in `ios-app/capacitor.config.json`, PR #41). Production PR #40 uses that token to refuse website (Stripe) purchases inside the app. CI proves the token in the simulator: the page's `navigator.userAgent` (native E2E phase A) and the HTTP `User-Agent` header of the WebView's page request (phase U). Keep it equal to the app's marketing version (`MARKETING_VERSION`); a unit test fails if they differ.

## 6. Owner-only steps, in order

1. Approve or rewrite the three purpose strings (§3) and the privacy-policy paragraph.
2. Create the App ID `com.restpilotai.app` with **HealthKit** (and later Associated Domains); create the App Store Connect record and the two subscriptions with their 2-week free intro offers (§5 B–D).
3. Decide the third-party AI consent screen (5.1.2(i)).
4. Approve the Amber pipeline change in §4 (or the GitHub fallback with your key).
5. `OWNER-SETUP.md` steps 1–5 (App Store Connect API key, private build repo, Codemagic, token, worker variables), then a TestFlight build for internal testers. Install it on a real iPhone: this is the first physical-device test of everything here.
6. App Store submission only after: the domain serves the Railway build (no Stripe), the AI consent exists, a demo account exists, and the device test passed.
